takeaways.skills: The test covers the 6 skill areas of mechanical CAD: work organisation, software and hardware, 3D modelling, rendering and animation, reverse engineering, and technical drawing.
takeaways.duration: The test takes about 90 minutes, and the timer can't be paused.
takeaways.ownSoftware: You work in your own CAD software on your own computer, then export and upload one file for each task.
takeaways.results: Results for 3D models come within minutes. Drawings are checked by a trainer.

software.autodeskTitle: Free for students: the Autodesk Education plan

autodesk.free: Inventor and Fusion are free for eligible students and educators through the Autodesk Education plan.
autodesk.year: The licence lasts one year, and you can renew it.
autodesk.verify: You must verify that you are a student. Have your student ID or enrolment letter ready.
autodesk.start: Verification can take time, so start today.

software.solidworksContact: Contact us for help getting a SOLIDWORKS licence
software.solidworksWhatsapp: Hi, I'm doing CAD Champions and I need help getting a SOLIDWORKS licence.

inventor.name: Inventor
inventor.suits: Everyone aiming for the competition. The competition tasks are built in Autodesk Inventor, so this is the best track to train on.
inventor.howToGet: Free with the Autodesk Education plan after you verify that you are a student.
inventor.duration: Verification: from minutes to a few days. Download and install: about 1 to 2 hours, because the download is large.

install.s1: Go to autodesk.com/education and create an Autodesk account with your school email if you have one.
install.s2: Ask for education access and upload your student ID or enrolment letter.
install.s3: Wait for the email that confirms you are verified.
install.s4: Sign in, find Inventor Professional on the education page and choose the newest version, your language and Windows 64-bit.
install.s5: Run the installer and keep the default options.
install.s6: Open Inventor and sign in with the same Autodesk account to activate it.

trouble.t1: Verification still pending after a few days? Check your spam folder, then upload a clearer document.
trouble.t2: Install stops or fails? Free at least 40 GB of disk space, restart, and run the installer again.
trouble.t3: Inventor asks you to sign in again? Use the same account you verified with.

fusion.name: Fusion
fusion.suits: Mac users and schools that already use Fusion. It is also allowed at some competitions, but Inventor is the main competition software.
fusion.howToGet: Free with the Autodesk Education plan after you verify that you are a student.
fusion.duration: Verification: from minutes to a few days. Download and install: about 30 minutes.

install.s1: Go to autodesk.com/education and create an Autodesk account.
install.s2: Ask for education access and upload your student ID or enrolment letter.
install.s3: When you are verified, find Fusion on the education page and download it.
install.s4: Run the installer. Fusion installs by itself and updates itself later.
install.s5: Open Fusion and sign in with the same Autodesk account.

trouble.t1: Fusion opens a free personal licence instead? Sign out and sign in with your verified education account.
trouble.t2: Fusion needs the internet to sign in. Open it once at home before test day.
trouble.t3: On a Mac, allow the installer in System Settings > Privacy & Security if macOS blocks it.

solidworks.name: SOLIDWORKS
solidworks.suits: Students and schools already working in SOLIDWORKS. The competition uses Autodesk Inventor or Fusion; this track builds the same skills, and we recommend switching to Inventor before the competition mock tests.
solidworks.howToGet: Through your school or a reseller's student offer.
solidworks.duration: Depends on your school or reseller. Install: about 1 hour.

install.s1: Ask your instructor if your school has SOLIDWORKS student licences.
install.s2: If not, ask a SOLIDWORKS reseller about student options.
install.s3: Download the installer with the serial number you receive.
install.s4: Run the installer, enter the serial number, and open SOLIDWORKS once to activate it.

trouble.t1: No serial number yet? Ask us on WhatsApp and we will help you find a licence.
trouble.t2: Activation fails? Check the date and time on your computer, then try again.

other.name: Other
other.suits: Students who already use another CAD program.
other.platforms: Any computer that runs your software.
other.howToGet: Any software is fine if it exports STEP files (AP214 or AP242) in millimetres.
other.duration: No install needed if you already have it.

install.s1: Open your software and check that File > Export (or Save As) offers STEP.
install.s2: Check that your model units can be set to millimetres.
install.s3: Do the practice upload in step 5 to make sure your export works.

trouble.t1: No STEP export? Use Fusion or Inventor for the test instead.

actions.intro: Tick each action when you can do it in your software. The step finishes when all 5 are ticked.
actions.phoneTip: Need to upload from your phone? Send the file to yourself (by email or a cloud drive such as Google Drive or OneDrive), open it on your phone, then upload it from there.
actions.densityHelp: Density is mass per volume. The test gives it for each part, for example steel 7850 kg/m³ and aluminium 2700 kg/m³.

units_mm.title: Set units to millimetres
units_mm.why: The test and the grader work in millimetres. Wrong units make every size wrong.
units_mm.mistake: Modelling in an inch template. A 50 mm cube drawn as 50 inches is 1270 mm, so the grader sees a part 25 times too big.

inventor.s1: Start each new part from the Standard (mm).ipt template (File > New).
inventor.s2: In an open part, go to Tools > Document Settings > Units.
inventor.s3: Set Length to millimeter and click OK.

fusion.s1: In the Browser on the left, open Document Settings.
fusion.s2: Hover over Units and click the pencil (Change Active Units).
fusion.s3: Choose Millimeter and click OK. To make it the default, set Preferences > Default Units > Design to mm.

solidworks.s1: Go to Tools > Options and open the Document Properties tab.
solidworks.s2: Click Units and choose MMGS (millimeter, gram, second).
solidworks.s3: Click OK. You can also check the unit system at the bottom right of the window.

material_density.title: Set the material and density
material_density.why: The test gives the density for each part, and the grader uses it to check your part's mass. Example: steel 7850 kg/m³, aluminium 2700 kg/m³.
material_density.mistake: Leaving the default (generic) material. Its density is not the one in the task, so your mass is wrong even when the shape is perfect.

inventor.s1: Right-click the part name in the model browser and open iProperties, then the Physical tab.
inventor.s2: Choose the material the task names, for example Steel.
inventor.s3: If the density is not the one in the task, open the Material Browser, copy the material and set its Density to the value given.
inventor.s4: Back on the Physical tab, click Update and check that the mass makes sense.

fusion.s1: Right-click the body in the Browser and choose Physical Material.
fusion.s2: Drag the material the task names (for example Steel) onto the body.
fusion.s3: If the density is not the one in the task, use Modify > Manage Materials to copy the material and edit its Density.
fusion.s4: Right-click the body and choose Properties to check the mass and volume.

solidworks.s1: In the FeatureManager tree, right-click Material and choose Edit Material.
solidworks.s2: Pick the material the task names, for example Plain Carbon Steel.
solidworks.s3: If the density is not the one in the task, copy the material to Custom Materials and set Mass density in kg/m^3.
solidworks.s4: Check the mass with Evaluate > Mass Properties.

export_step.title: Export a STEP file
export_step.why: STEP (AP214 or AP242) is the file the grader reads. Export one file per task and check that it ends in .step or .stp.
export_step.mistake: Uploading the native file (.ipt, .f3d, .sldprt) or renaming a file to .step. Renaming does not convert the file - only Export does.

inventor.s1: Go to File > Export > CAD Format.
inventor.s2: Set Save as type to STEP Files (*.stp, *.ste, *.step).
inventor.s3: Click Options and choose Application Protocol 214 or 242.
inventor.s4: Name the file after the task (for example Task1_Plate.step) and click Save.

fusion.s2: Set Type to STEP Files (*.stp) and tick Save to my computer.
fusion.s3: Choose a folder, name the file after the task and click Export.

solidworks.s2: Set Save as type to STEP AP214 or STEP AP242 (*.step; *.stp).
solidworks.s3: Name the file after the task and click Save.

export_pdf.title: Export a drawing as PDF
export_pdf.why: Drawings are uploaded as PDF. Use the correct sheet size and include all pages.
export_pdf.mistake: Exporting only the current sheet, or shrinking an A3 drawing onto A4. Open the PDF and check every page and the sheet size before you upload.

inventor.s2: Go to File > Export > Export to PDF and click Options.
inventor.s3: Choose All Sheets, keep the sheet size of the drawing, then Save.

fusion.s1: Open your drawing in the Drawing workspace.
fusion.s2: Click Export PDF in the toolbar.
fusion.s3: Choose all sheets, then export and save the PDF.

solidworks.s2: Go to File > Save As and set Save as type to Adobe Portable Document Format (*.pdf).
solidworks.s3: Make sure all sheets are included, then Save.

find_upload.title: Find your files and upload them
find_upload.why: During the timed test you must find each export fast and upload it straight away.
find_upload.mistake: Uploading an older export by mistake. Name every file with its task number, and keep only the latest export in your test folder.

inventor.s1: Inventor exports to your project folder unless you choose another. Look at the folder in the Export window before you click Save.
inventor.s2: Make one folder for the test (for example on your Desktop) and export every file there.
inventor.s3: On the upload box, click Choose file and open that folder.

fusion.s1: Fusion keeps designs in the cloud. Export saves a copy to the folder you choose.
fusion.s2: Make one folder for the test (for example on your Desktop) and choose it every time you export.
fusion.s3: On the upload box, click Choose file and open that folder.

solidworks.s1: Save As uses the part's own folder unless you choose another. Look at the folder before you click Save.
solidworks.s2: Make one folder for the test (for example on your Desktop) and save every export there.
solidworks.s3: On the upload box, click Choose file and open that folder.

practice.task: Model a 50 x 50 x 50 mm cube in steel (7850 kg/m³) and upload it as STEP.
practice.untimed: This practice has no timer, nothing counts, and you can try as many times as you like.
practice.rulesTitle: To pass, your file must be:
practice.stubNote: For now we check that your file is a real STEP export. Full checks of units, solids and volume are coming soon.
practice.passBody: Your export and upload work. You are ready for the real files.
practice.tryAgain: Fix the file and upload it again. There is no limit on tries.
practice.unavailableTitle: We couldn't check your file right now
practice.unavailableBody: Your file uploaded, but our checker is not available. Try again in a few minutes.
practice.errorBody: We couldn't finish the check. Try uploading again.

demo.briefToast: In the real test, this downloads the task drawing.

timer.title: The timer
timer.body: It runs on our server. Closing the page does not pause it. You get warnings at 15, 5 and 1 minute.

tasks.title: The task list
tasks.body: Every task and its status. Pick a task to open it. A green check means its file is uploaded.

brief.title: The brief and drawing
brief.body: Read the task here and download the drawing. The material and density are in the brief.

upload.title: The upload box
upload.body: Upload one file per task as soon as you finish it. You can replace it until you submit.

submit.title: Submit test
submit.body: Press it when every task has a file. When time runs out, the test is submitted for you.

demo.doneBody: On test day, everything will be where you just saw it.
